conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be helping take care of you during this stay. Can you tell me what brought you in today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I came because my hearing suddenly dropped in my right ear about four days ago. It started like I was underwater, then felt like cotton was stuffed in it, and now I can’t hear anything. It’s painful too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any drainage from the ear or fever?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No drainage, and I haven’t had a fever. But I’ve also been having this new pain that shoots down my left arm when I move my neck or shoulder.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks for letting me know. We’re also following up on that nasopharyngeal mass seen on your last CT. You don’t have sore throat or trouble swallowing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, my throat feels fine. No pain there. But I’m worried—could this be lymphoma coming back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a valid concern. Your history makes us cautious, but your last PET scan and bone marrow biopsy were negative. Still, we’ll keep investigating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad those were clear. But this ear thing is really scaring me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. The fluid in your middle ear is likely due to the mass pressing on the Eustachian tube. It’s not infected now, but it’s causing pressure and hearing loss.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not an ear infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not at this point. No signs of bacterial infection. ENT will follow up after discharge to monitor it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that helps. What about the shoulder pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did an X-ray today. It looked normal—no fracture or dislocation. But we’re ordering an MRI tomorrow to get a better look.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Could it be related to the lymphoma?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly, but your oncologist thinks it’s more likely musculoskeletal. The MRI will help us decide.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. I’ve been on a lot of meds—do I need to change anything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve reviewed your list. You’re on acyclovir, methadone, glimepiride, metformin, and others. We’ll keep them running as before unless something changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. My blood sugar’s been a little high lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We saw your glucose was 295 this morning. We’ll monitor it and adjust insulin if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. We’re going to do a biopsy of the nasopharyngeal mass today. It’s similar to the one you had before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is it necessary? I thought the last one was inconclusive.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, because the mass is still there. The earlier biopsy showed some atypical cells with CD30 and EBV markers, but no clear cancer. This time, we hope for more tissue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if it’s not cancer, what else could it be?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It could be a reactive process—your immune system overresponding due to infection or inflammation, especially with your CVID.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The biopsy went well. They got a good sample. Pathology will take a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Any fluid or pus?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They found cystic fluid, but no malignant cells. It wasn’t sent for culture.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So not an abscess?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not clearly. The imaging suggested it, but the fluid didn’t look infected. You’re not on antibiotics now because you’re not febrile or systemically ill.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We swabbed your throat yesterday to check for herpes or shingles. The results came back negative.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had mouth ulcers before—could that be related?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked. No HSV or VZV. Likely unrelated to the current issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your shoulder MRI is back. It shows tendinosis in the rotator cuff and some thickening of ligaments—consistent with adhesive capsulitis, or 'frozen shoulder.'

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So not cancer?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No lymphoma involvement. No joint infection either. It’s a strain, likely from overuse or posture.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What’s the treatment?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Physical therapy first. If that doesn’t help, your PCP can consider a steroid injection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I can do that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The pathology from the biopsy is still pending. But so far, no signs of active infection or clear malignancy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But they saw reactive cells?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, a cluster of reactive cells that look suspicious, but not diagnostic. We’ll need follow-up with ENT and oncology to monitor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I’m not in danger now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re stable. No fever, no worsening symptoms. That’s why we’re planning to discharge you tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need more tests?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. ENT will see you for the ear fluid and mass. And your oncologist will review the biopsy results when they’re final.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—we’re discharging you today. Your condition is stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No changes to my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: None. Keep taking everything as before. And please keep your follow-up appointments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. If your hearing doesn’t improve or the shoulder pain worsens, call your doctor right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. I feel much better just knowing it’s not an active infection or cancer right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re glad. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're welcome. The nurse will go over discharge instructions and get you ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, I’m ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your blood counts are still low, but stable. That’s likely from your CVID and past treatments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know, I’ve had that for years. As long as it’s not getting worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’ll monitor it with your regular doctors.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll be in touch if anything changes with your results.
